newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Share shortage pushes Moroccan bourse higher.
newsitem.headline: Share shortage pushes Moroccan bourse higher.

text.p: The Casablanca stock market closed on Friday 2.9 percent higher with most stocks pushed higher by a shortage of shares, a stockbroker said.
The all-share index closed at 555.22 points from 539.22 last Friday.
"Fertima, Samir and Sonasid, traded under the new electronic system, tended to rise," a broker at BMCI Securities said.
The exchange earlier this week started the gradual introduction of electronic trading, initially with shares of four companies, including.
ONA group the biggest private holding closed at 701 dirhams from 690 dirhams last week.
In the banking sector, Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur slipped to 490 dirhams from 495 dirhams.
Earlier this week, it was reported to have shown a net profit of 366 million dirhams ($38.9 million) for 1996, up 21 percent on the 301 million dirhams of 1995.
Leading stock Wafabank traded at 725 dirhams from 690 dirhams.
Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique closed at 190 dirhams from 185 dirhams last week.
Leasing firm Maroc-Leasing which was listed on the bourse late in February took seven dirhams on the week to close at 271 dirhams from 264 dirhams. Its initial price was 230 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest conglomerate which holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, closed at 665 dirhams from 666 dirhams last Friday.
Brewery firm Brasseries du Maroc fell to 1864 dirhams from 1921 dirhams last week.
Newly-floated credit firm Credor rose to 645 dirhams from 630 dirhams last week.
Traded volume on the official market on Friday was 49.6 million dirhams from 77.4 million dirhams last Friday.
